sample_unit: scripted consultation sessions (end-to-end arm; 385 in intrinsic arm)
models_evaluated: ambient AI scribe (ASR plus LLM note generation)
languages: 77 languages including high-, medium-, and low-resource languages

links.outcome: End-to-end serious note error incidence by language resource tier
links.effect: End-to-end serious errors rose with language scarcity (high 7%, medium 10%, low 15%; OR 1.54 per tier, 95% CI 1.15-2.07; p=0.004), whereas intrinsic note generation showed no detectable language gradient.
links.quote: End-to-end serious errors rose steeply with complexity (L1 1% to L4/L5 24%) and language scarcity (high 7%, medium 10%, low 15%; OR 1.54 per tier, 95% CI 1.15-2.07; p=0.004, GEE clustered on language).

links.outcome: Serious errors, including ASR-derived and note-originated, in ambient scribe notes
links.effect: Intrinsic serious-error rate 3.4%; of serious in-note errors in end-to-end, 87% ASR-derived and 7% note-originated; amplification exceeded correction threefold.
links.quote: Of serious in-note errors, 87% were ASR-derived and 7% note-originated; amplification exceeded correction threefold (fate entropy 1.19 bits).

links.outcome: Whether component-level performance predicts end-to-end note risk
links.effect: Low serious-error rates in individual layers (3.4% intrinsic) did not preclude higher end-to-end note risk (up to 24% at L4/L5); component-level metrics could not fully capture risk.
links.quote: Low serious-error rates in individual layers did not preclude higher end-to-end note risk.

links.outcome: Reproducibility of note generation across repeated runs
links.effect: Repeated generation showed moderate reproducibility (Fleiss kappa 0.42).
links.quote: Repeated generation showed moderate reproducibility (Fleiss kappa 0.42); word error rate explained 24% of cross-language variance versus ∼1% for transcription risk density.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating end-to-end clinician-facing note rather than component-level metrics alone
Root-cause taxonomy attributing note errors to ASR versus note-generation origin

screen.reason: Empirical benchmarking study evaluating clinical safety risk across components (ASR vs. LLM note generation) and end-to-end performance of a multilingual ambient scribe, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
